profile.summary: Full stack developer with experience in managing and securing highly confidential data. Also, have an interest in high performance/throughput applications as well as gaming!

positions.title: Software Development Engineer II
positions.description: Developed UI tools for artists. Also in game UI features and screens for Forza Motorsport

positions.title: Full Stack Engineer
positions.description: Develop web and mobile features for millions of Chase users. Also developed a separate site for users to submit data requests to Chase.

positions.title: Lead Full Stack Engineer
positions.description:
designed, lead a dev team, and developed  secure web applications with Java, Spring Boot, and Vaadin for banking teams to manage conflicts of interest.
I also set up infra, code pipeline, and automated deployment.

positions.title: System Engineer
positions.description:
Support various applications.
Manage, debug, and solve production issues.
Devised algorithm to manage increasing server load due to developers creating excessive production processes.
Created web app to better manage developer pushes to production.

positions.title: Software Developer Intern
positions.description:
Develop Windows 8 metro apps in C# and XAML
Build web apps with Django and AngularJS

positions.title: Summer Technology Analyst - Systems Engineer
positions.description:
Develop web pages using Perl and the Catalyst web framework to help efficiency and reporting capability of my team. Also, used python to transfer data from excel to MySQL and MSSQL and used that data for the web pages.

Used JQuery, Bootstrap, DataTables, and various other js plugins to complete my tasks.

• Team Leader

projects.title: Measure180
projects.description:
•	Windows Phone 8 app that measures distances and heights by pointing the phone’s camera at an object.

•	Link: http://www.windowsphone.com/en-us/store/app/measure180/864c53bd-3eae-472b-8628-4d109352d6c8

•	First C#/.NET app I made so the code is jumbled and not efficiently done, but it works. Like they always say “If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it.” Core code of the app is found in MainPage.xaml.cs
